Looking at the data across all 5 examples, I notice some consistent patterns:

1. **Forecast bias - systematically too low (conservative)**
Looking at Example 1:
- Model forecasts start around 76.06-76.59
- True outcomes start around 76.02-76.79
The model is actually quite close at the beginning but then diverges

Let me look more carefully. In Example 1, the model forecast on day 1 is 76.06 but true is 76.02 - very close. But by day 9-10, model is 78.74-79.35 while true is 78.31-79.16.

Actually, let me re-examine. Looking at the pattern:

Example 1 model forecasts vs true:
Day 1: 76.06 vs 76.02 (off by +0.04)
Day 2: 75.99 vs 75.76 (off by +0.23)
Day 3: 76.39 vs 75.98 (off by +0.41)
Day 4: 77.31 vs 76.79 (off by +0.52)
Day 5: 76.21 vs 75.72 (off by +0.49)
Day 6: 76.71 vs 76.33 (off by +0.38)
Day 7: 77.69 vs 77.43 (off by +0.26)
Day 8: 79.35 vs 79.16 (off by +0.19)
Day 9: 79.02 vs 78.75 (off by +0.27)
Day 10: 78.74 vs 78.31 (off by +0.43)

The model appears to be **systematically too high** compared to the early days, but then catches up? No wait, let me look at example 2:

The initial deviations are more pronounced, around +0.25 to +0.80, which gradually decrease to +0.10-0.30 by later days.
